statement: Each of the $12$ students in a class writes down the names of exactly $3$ classmates they would like to work with. Two students form a match if each wrote down the other's name. A name on a list is called one-sided if the student named did not write down the writer's name. There are exactly $7$ matches. How many of the names written down are one-sided?

choices.misconception: I counted the names that belong to matches, 2 for each of the 7 matches, instead of the names that are one-sided.
I thought exactly half of the 36 names had to be one-sided, but nothing in the problem says that.
I subtracted one name for each match, 36 - 7 = 29, but each match is made of two names, one on each list.
I counted every name written down, 12 times 3 = 36, and forgot to take away the names that are part of matches.

hints: First count all the names written down.
Every name is either one-sided or part of a match. How many names does one match use?
There are $12 \cdot 3 = 36$ names. Each match uses $2$ names (one on each student's list), so the $7$ matches use $14$ names.

solutions.reliable: The students write $12 \cdot 3 = 36$ names in all. A match between two students uses exactly two of those names: each student's name on the other's list. The $7$ matches use $7 \cdot 2 = 14$ names, and every other name is one-sided. So $36 - 14 = 22$ names are one-sided.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
